nodes.label: OTA milestone and source map
nodes.rationale: Maps the architecture, publisher, client, staging, automatic review, replay and owner release procedures. As of 2026-10-28 Android code 4 and iOS build 4 were delivered with production OTA ON to test tracks, not public store release.

nodes.label: Per-file release delivery
nodes.rationale: Individual files support hash-verified reuse and resumable downloads without KMP archive readers or archive attack defenses; roughly 400 first-install requests require measured performance gates.
nodes.source_location: D2 — A manifest of individual files, not a snapshot archive

nodes.label: Pinned ECDSA catalog trust chain
nodes.rationale: P-256/SHA-256 over exact DSSE PAE bytes uses built-in Android/JVM and iOS crypto without a Swift bridge; manifest and file hashes extend authenticity, while sequence and expiry resist replay and freeze.
nodes.source_location: D3 — Authenticity: ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over DSSE PAE, two pinned keys

nodes.label: Static content-addressed OTA delivery
nodes.rationale: A single signed mutable catalog points to immutable SHA-256 blobs, enabling atomic publication, shared files, provider portability and rollback without an always-on backend.
nodes.source_location: D1 — Static, content-addressed delivery with one signed catalog per channel

nodes.label: Archive delivery deferred to contract v2
nodes.norm_label: archive delivery deferred to contract v2
nodes.rationale: Batching changes closed wire shapes and compromises per-file reuse, resume and validation; reconsider only if parallelism and gzip still fail measured device thresholds.

nodes.label: Android staging smoke protocol
nodes.rationale: Separate .otastaging debug app exercises Android TLS, noBackupFilesDir, Activity/process lifecycle and UI over local or VK HTTPS; staging settings are barred from store release builds.

nodes.label: Bundled-floor limitations in device testing
nodes.rationale: Bundled 70450 means catalog rollback to 70374 stays above the bundled floor and downloads mostly manifests; a historical APK excluding 70450 is needed to prove full network delivery.
nodes.source_location: 2. What a device can and cannot show today

nodes.label: Owner-controlled Android OTA build switch
nodes.rationale: Only enabled=true activates production configuration and INTERNET in release/play merged manifests. OTA OFF preserves saved records, but unbundled OTA-only builds remain unavailable until their data returns.

nodes.label: Pinned Android production configuration
nodes.rationale: Production origin https://ota.mythweld.com and primary/backup keyring are fixed and checked by Gradle and runtime; staging/test keys, substituted origins and production trust anchors are rejected.

nodes.label: Automatic candidate preparation
nodes.rationale: Combines publishable index, bundled product and verified production catalog; disposable clones run the existing pipeline and gates, retaining PREPARED artifacts while BLOCKED/UNKNOWN runs retry. Preparation never publishes and G1 merge remains required.

nodes.label: Verified automatic candidate review PR
nodes.rationale: A separate propose job validates strict reports, bundle ancestry, authorship and allowed regular-file scope, then updates ota-candidate branches idempotently; reviewer commits cause CONFLICT and GITHUB_TOKEN-created PRs need owner-triggered CI.

nodes.label: Preparation pipeline dependency ordering
nodes.rationale: Normalize talents before visuals fetch because icons are resolved from the dataset; tooltip normalization precedes localization. Forced replays of committed builds had hidden the new-build ordering defect.

nodes.label: Atomic install, activation and staging resume
nodes.norm_label: atomic install, activation and staging resume
nodes.rationale: Verified staging files survive interruption and are rehashed before reuse; rename installs a release and atomic state replacement activates it. Local recovery precedes UI and never treats unreadable state as permission to delete releases.
nodes.source_location: 4.1 Startup; 4.3 Install and activate; 4.7 Staging, resume and recovery

nodes.label: Historical dataset resolution and safe retention
nodes.norm_label: historical dataset resolution and safe retention
nodes.rationale: Resolve exact saved-build identity through installed, bundled, then accepted-catalog on-demand data with typed Retry failures. Keep active/previous, referenced unbundled builds and leased releases; unreadable library prevents installed-release deletion.

nodes.label: Immutable leased DatasetSnapshot sessions
nodes.rationale: Existing repositories reuse DatasetAssetSource routing per build. New sessions see activated data; open editors keep immutable sources and leased releases so retention cannot delete their datasets.

nodes.label: Content-addressed catalog payload commit protocol
nodes.rationale: Accepted payload bytes are synced under their hash before the single state commit; cleanup follows state write, preventing a crash from pairing old state with overwritten or missing catalog bytes.

nodes.label: Strict common JSON and platform verification
nodes.norm_label: strict common json and platform verification
nodes.rationale: A bounded raw-byte lexer validates RFC 8259 and duplicate names before typed decoding; canonical model-tree comparison rejects coercion, and common SPKI/DER checks prevent malformed-input differences across native crypto APIs.

nodes.norm_label: warm reuse lost to png re-encoding
nodes.rationale: Only six files match between releases A and B despite unchanged icon source content; platform-dependent PNG encoding makes warm download resemble cold, while resumed installs correctly request only missing files.

nodes.label: Publisher implementation brief
nodes.rationale: Build deterministic releases from committed data, reuse reference verification and mechanics gates, upload/read-back blobs before the catalog, require explicit execution, and support offline local-store rehearsal.

nodes.label: Non-overridable publisher STOP boundary
nodes.rationale: Only G5 warnings and G7 live evidence may be accepted by approval records; G6 unsupported mechanics and every other STOP remain unpublishable under any flag, environment or configuration.

nodes.rationale: Pure shared verification and policies combine with composeApp platform adapters and orchestration; local startup, verified resumable install, atomic activation and historical resolution preserve existing builds.

nodes.label: Interleaved retry-control measurement
nodes.rationale: Healthy-origin cold installs succeeded 30/30 per arm; injected connection loss yielded retry 20/20 versus control 11/20 first-check installs. No real failures occurred, so reliability improvement is injected-loss evidence, not observed VK loss.

nodes.label: Bounded per-request transfer retry
nodes.rationale: GET transfers may repeat twice after 0.5 s and 2 s with a 10 s Android/JVM connect timeout; the same URL, byte limits and integrity checks remain enforced within one attempt.

nodes.label: libjpeg-turbo compatible IJG and Modified BSD licenses
nodes.norm_label: libjpeg-turbo compatible ijg and modified bsd licenses
nodes.rationale: IJG covers libjpeg API and inherited/modified code; zlib SIMD terms are subsumed in that context. TurboJPEG API and build system use Modified 3-clause BSD; TurboJPEG wrapping libjpeg brings both license scopes.

nodes.label: libjpeg-turbo source and binary distribution notices
nodes.norm_label: libjpeg-turbo source and binary distribution notices
nodes.rationale: The explanatory roll-up calls for retaining source notices and marking modifications; binary/static distribution documents acknowledge IJG and reproduce Modified BSD when TurboJPEG is used. Project/contributor endorsement names are restricted; warranty/liability disclaimers remain.

nodes.label: Dual licenses preserve attribution and endorsement protections
nodes.norm_label: dual licenses preserve attribution and endorsement protections
nodes.rationale: Modified BSD extends attribution and endorsement protections to the libjpeg-turbo Project's new code, protections IJG wording gives only to IJG-derived work.

nodes.label: Owner-applied VK Cloud OTA hosting templates
nodes.norm_label: owner-applied vk cloud ota hosting templates
nodes.rationale: Configuration is applied manually by the owner; repository tools do not create, change or delete cloud resources; production-deployment.md owns the procedure.

nodes.label: Production catalog and content-addressed blob policy
nodes.norm_label: production catalog and content-addressed blob policy
nodes.rationale: Anonymous GetObject is restricted to catalog and blobs; credentials stay outside git; s3_channels.py defines the production profile and production-key tests synchronize templates.

nodes.label: Design authority precedence
nodes.rationale: UX/UI V1 pages 2–3 wins conflicts; otherwise B3 owns Talent Tree behavior. Immutable PDFs feed cited, spec-pinned design token derivatives.

nodes.label: Portrait inspector reading-state refinement
nodes.rationale: First selection is compact; user-expanded or collapsed state persists across subsequent selections and rank/history changes, with new descriptions at top. Show returns compact; state is view-only.

nodes.label: Continue-first Home hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Returning Home prioritizes Continue, three recent builds and All builds, with New build pinned in the thumb zone. New-user Home uses one sentence and action without placeholder cards; first preparation uses determinate progress and disables New build until ready.

nodes.label: Recency-sorted row library with thresholded discovery
nodes.norm_label: recency-sorted row library with thresholded discovery
nodes.rationale: Rows carry identity, spec split and inline data badges with overflow as their only row control. Last-edited ordering is fixed; search appears at 13+ builds and class chips require both 13+ builds and 2+ classes. Empty state offers one create action.

nodes.label: Frozen Talent Tree interaction contract
nodes.rationale: Tap selects; visible controls spend/refund; Show moves one prerequisite hop; independent selection styling; portrait bottom and landscape side inspectors.

nodes.label: Private NDA corpus exclusion
nodes.rationale: The private ceremony directory must never be traversed, read or indexed and must remain excluded from Git and graphify; knowledge-graph maintenance cannot ingest this material.
